facts.claim: NSW: marriage celebrants have up to 14 days to register a marriage with the NSW Registry, and the quickest way to receive the certificate is for the celebrant to register online. A standard marriage certificate costs AUD 70 standard service or AUD 105 priority (fees include AUD 11 postage and handling, current as of 1 July 2026). Processing: certificate applied for by the celebrant within 2 months of registration up to 3 weeks; online application up to 3 weeks (priority up to 2 weeks); postal up to 4 weeks; via Service NSW up to 4 weeks; plus 5 to 7 days postage. Official plus commemorative package AUD 100; commemorative only AUD 44. Sending a certificate to a passport office costs AUD 51.
facts.publisher: NSW Government, Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, Fees and processing times
facts.use_note: Fees current as of 1 July 2026 (FY 2026-27). A secondary search snippet showed an older AUD 67/99; the live page reads AUD 70/105.

facts.claim: NSW: registration of a change of name for an adult costs AUD 203 standard or AUD 233 priority (registration only); the change of name certificate at time of registration is a further AUD 70. Security checks can take up to 10 business days before processing.
facts.publisher: NSW Government, Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, Fees and processing times
facts.use_note: Only relevant where a formal change of name is needed (see F-111, F-112).

facts.claim: VIC: a legal certificate (original or replacement birth, death, marriage, change of name or single status) costs AUD 59.10, effective 1 July 2026, plus AUD 10.60 express post within Australia (international express AUD 58.60). Change of name registration costs AUD 148.60, which includes the AUD 59.10 legal certificate; the AUD 89.50 registration part is non-refundable. Fees are updated every financial year. Payment by card, BPAY or money order; no cash.
facts.publisher: Births, Deaths and Marriages Victoria, Fees
facts.use_note: Page updated 23 Sep 2026. A third-party snippet quoted AUD 57.50 and AUD 87.10 (older schedule); use the live figures.

facts.claim: QLD: the authorised celebrant registers the marriage on the couple's behalf and has 14 days to submit it. The Registry does not send an official certificate when a marriage is registered; you must apply and pay. There are three types: the official marriage certificate (proves the relationship and can be used for change of family name through marriage), the commemorative certificate and the ceremonial certificate given by the celebrant, neither of which can be used to prove the relationship.
facts.publisher: Queensland Government, Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, Get a marriage certificate
facts.use_note: 14-day timing per the QLD search result for https://www.qld.gov.au/law/births-deaths-marriages-and-divorces/marriage-weddings-and-civil-partnerships/marriage/registering-a-marriage (page not fetched; snippet only). The three-certificate wording is the clearest official statement for the article's explainer.

facts.claim: QLD: official marriage certificate AUD 58.10; commemorative package including one official certificate AUD 75.60; urgent application AUD 34.45 extra. Standard processing up to 10 business days, urgent within 2 business days. Regular postage free; registered post AUD 8.10, express AUD 8.55, international registered AUD 21.55. Apply online, by post, at a Magistrates Court or QGAP office, via some JPs in the Community, or at the Brisbane registry.
facts.publisher: Queensland Government, Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, Get a marriage certificate
facts.use_note: Third-party sites quote AUD 54 or AUD 67; ignore.

facts.claim: WA: a WA marriage certificate costs AUD 60.00 including regular post; priority fee AUD 44.00 extra including express post. Standard processing up to 2 working days plus postage; priority within 24 hours. Available to the married couple; the marriage must be registered in WA. Apply by post, in person at the Perth Registry (Level 10, 141 St Georges Terrace) or a courthouse; faxed or emailed applications not accepted.
facts.publisher: Government of Western Australia, Department of Justice, Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, BDM3 Marriage Certificate Application Form (updated August 2026)
facts.use_note: Online ordering also exists per search results but not read.

facts.claim: SA: a certificate is issued only if the marriage was registered in South Australia. Standard marriage certificate AUD 72.00; standard and commemorative AUD 99.00. Priority (fast track) fee AUD 50.00, processed within 1 business day. Apply online, by post or in person at Service SA centres; not by phone.
facts.publisher: SA.GOV.AU (Attorney-General's Department), Apply for a marriage or relationship certificate
facts.use_note: Standard processing times are on the CBS website (not read).

facts.claim: TAS: standard certificate (birth, death, marriage, change of name or relationship) AUD 60.76; priority service AUD 43.12 extra, issued within 24 hours of an approved application. Registered post AUD 7.55, express AUD 9.00. Change of name registration including the certificate AUD 237.16.
facts.publisher: Tasmanian Government, Department of Justice, Births, Deaths and Marriages, Fees
facts.use_note: A search snippet showed AUD 57.97 (older); the live page reads AUD 60.76, last updated 1 July 2026.

facts.claim: NT: marriage certificate AUD 74; change of name certificate AUD 74; priority fee AUD 39; total change of name fee AUD 148.
facts.publisher: Northern Territory Government, Births, Deaths and Marriages office fees
facts.use_note: Page is undated, so medium. Write 'AUD 74 (NT BDM fee page, checked November 2026)'.

facts.claim: ACT: you can request a marriage certificate online if you are named on it or authorised by a named person; requests carry an application fee unless a hardship waiver applies, and need 3 proofs of identity. Certificate types: a standard certificate on security paper, the only type recognised as the official registered marriage certificate and commonly accepted as proof of identity; a commemorative certificate on normal paper, not typically recognised as a legal document; and a package of both.
facts.publisher: Access Canberra (ACT Government), Request a marriage certificate
facts.use_note: Fee amount not shown on this page; the ACT forms and fees page timed out. ACT fee: not published in this batch (see N-100).

facts.claim: Across registries, the celebrant's presentation (ceremonial) certificate is not the legal record: QLD says the ceremonial certificate from the celebrant cannot be used to prove the relationship (F-103); ACT says only the standard certificate is the official registered marriage certificate (F-109); NSW, VIC, SA and TAS sell commemorative certificates separately from the official or legal certificate (F-100, F-102, F-106, F-107).
facts.publisher: Queensland Government, Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages (with cross-references to other registry pages)
facts.use_note: Synthesis of official facts already listed; cite the individual registry pages in the table. Federal rule that celebrants have 14 days to lodge is confirmed on NSW and QLD pages only; other states not read, write 'within 14 days (NSW and QLD registries)' or cite the Marriage Act if batch A has it.

facts.claim: Australian Passport Office: if you change your family name because of marriage you may keep your current passport or get a new one. For a new passport in a spouse's family name you link names with your Australian birth or citizenship certificate plus a marriage certificate issued by an Australian RBDM, a registered relationship certificate, or an RBDM name change certificate. A name change certificate is always required if you changed given names, or if you were born in Australia and married overseas. Foreign certificates are accepted only if you cannot get an Australian equivalent and must be legalised and fully translated.
facts.publisher: Australian Passport Office (DFAT), Change of name or gender
facts.use_note: Name-change answer for the article: for a marriage in Australia, the official registry marriage certificate (not the celebrant's) is enough to take a spouse's surname in a passport. Hyphenated or combined names: the page says 'taken your spouse or partner's family name, or added it to your own family name', so adding is covered; other forms not covered.

facts.claim: VIC BDM: if you married in Australia you do not need to apply for a change of name with BDM to take your spouse's family name; give organisations a copy of your Australian marriage certificate. Most organisations only accept the BDM-issued legal certificate, not the ceremonial one, and some may require a BDM change of name. An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia.
facts.publisher: Births, Deaths and Marriages Victoria, Changing your name after marriage, separation or divorce
facts.use_note: Medium: read via search-result summary, page not fetched in full. Consistent with NSW policy (previous batch, https://www.nsw.gov.au/family-and-relationships/name-changes-and-corrections/change-of-name/change-of-name-policy: a person legally married in Australia can take their spouse's family name without registering a change of name) and QLD (F-103: official certificate usable for change of family name through marriage). WA, SA, TAS, ACT, NT name-change pages: not read in this batch; write 'not published here' rather than assume.

legal.summary: Passport in married name: Australian RBDM marriage certificate links names; Australian-born person married overseas needs an RBDM name change certificate. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Celebrant registers the marriage within 14 days; official certificate must be applied for separately; ceremonial certificate is not proof. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
No BDM change of name needed to take spouse's surname after an Australian marriage; use the legal certificate. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
